summary: Wenatchee NF summit in Yakima County: a 1925 cupola cabin, then a 42-foot L-4 tower (1934 or 1935) removed in 1966; photo captions label footings and a drive-up road.

facts.design: 42-foot wooden tower with an L-4 cab, replacing a D-6 cupola cabin built in 1925
facts.status_note: Tower removed in 1966 per the register and Willhite; firelookout.com says destroyed. Willhite's photo captions label tower footings.

staffing.as_of: 1960 (last staffing found in the sources read)

access.note: Drive-up per Willhite: Ahtanum Road from Yakama into Ahtanum State Forest, passable until the last two miles. The summit sits where National Forest, state forest and Yakama Nation land meet, so check ownership before going.

visit.trail_note: No tower stands to climb. Hiking books suggest walking the last part from Clover Flats campground, a distance of 2 miles, per Willhite.

events.note: The 42-foot wooden L-4 tower replaced the cupola, per the register and firelookout.com. Willhite dates the tower to 1934.
The old cupola was trucked to the Blue Slide lookout site
Juanita Ward left for Darland Mountain to spend the summer at the lookout station, per a July 3, 1958 Goldendale Sentinel item quoted by Willhite
A September 1, 1960 Goldendale Sentinel item, quoted by Willhite, describes a young woman attending the lookout who spent her winters in Ellensburg attending college
The register and Willhite say the L-4 tower was removed; firelookout.com says destroyed
Registered July 19, 2012 as FFLOS US 1360, WA 260

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and firelookout.com give 1935 for the 42-foot L-4 tower; Willhite gives 1934. Not resolved; the story gives both.
The register and Willhite say the L-4 tower was removed in 1966; firelookout.com says it was destroyed that year. Both are reported.

notes_for_editor: Tower year conflicts: register and firelookout.com 1935, Willhite 1934 (his page also dates panorama photos to 1934). Removal versus destruction in 1966 is reported both ways. The 1924 forestry report quoted on Willhite's and Forest Lookouts' pages does not name Darland Mountain in the quoted text, so it is left out. A 1955 photo caption naming lookout Barbara Vanderlaan is left out because the year is not clearly tied to it. Staffing names come from 1950s and 1960s newspaper items as Willhite and Forest Lookouts quote them; I did not check the originals. Access 'public' rests on Willhite's drive-up description; he places the summit where National Forest, state forest and Yakama Nation land meet, so an editor should check whether any part is tribal land. The record's kind 'tower' and elevation 2127.8 m match the register's 2,128 m. Used 4 page reads (1 grep read of the Forest Lookouts page), 1 WebSearch.
